scope: Three image proposals only; not a complete replacement release package

concepts.A: Fake recruiter facade hides theft. Identity deception; payoff opening. Candidate title: The Fake Job Interview That Cost Binance $6 Billion.
concepts.B: Closed vault versus independent money exit. Failed emergency stop; payoff 01:13. Candidate title: Binance Stopped Withdrawals. The Theft Kept Going.
concepts.C: Intact frozen money inaccessible to recipient. Frozen vs returned; payoff 01:49. Candidate title: Billions Frozen. But Were They Recovered?

distinction: A vs B: deceptive human interaction vs failed system shutdown. A vs C: trust exploited vs inaccessible assets. B vs C: active outflow vs immobilized assets. Titles ask about entry, continued theft, and recovery respectively.

prompts.A: Use case: ads-marketing. Create a NEW 16:9 YouTube thumbnail for Paper Detour. Use the reference ONLY for premium handcrafted paper/card material, sculpted faces, tactile edges, contact shadows, and dimensional lettering. Do NOT copy its layout, mountains, glowing roads, desk props, hooded host or orange-purple palette. One coherent bold editorial paper diorama, not photoreal or glossy CGI. Large immediate forms readable at 320x180. No decorative outer border. All headline text must be generated in the image, exact spelling, large wide cut-paper letters. Reserve bottom right from important text. This is an unmistakably stylized metaphor, not documentary evidence. Scene: an enormous upright video interview screen fills the right half. A charming paper recruiter face on it is a flat stage facade being peeled aside, revealing a dark gloved hand behind it grabbing a stack of gold crypto tokens. On the left foreground, a trusting engineer in a plain light shirt reaching toward the screen with a job application; his face and gesture large, adult human proportions. The dramatic reveal of deception should dominate, not technical symbols. Modern hiring context from the video-call screen, no need to read tiny UI. Mint/ivory office facade against deep crimson behind it. Exact editorial headline in two lines: 'FAKE INTERVIEW' / 'REAL $6B THEFT'. The $6B is rounded theft valuation, not a salary or bribe. Do not imply the engineer knowingly gave money; stealing hand belongs behind the deceptive recruiter facade. No other words.
